QF.id: Income, Residential Status, Five Heads of Income_23

question.text: Mr. Sanjay's gross salary is Rs.15,00,000. Under the new tax regime, he claims the standard deduction of Rs.75,000. His employer contributes 14% of his basic salary (Rs.10,00,000) to NPS under section 80CCD(2). What is his net taxable salary income?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook computation pattern first adds the employer NPS contribution to salary as a perquisite, then subtracts the standard deduction, and finally allows the 80CCD(2) deduction up to the 14% new-regime limit. Salary as offered: Rs.15,00,000. Add: Employer NPS contribution = 14% of Rs.10,00,000 = Rs.1,40,000. Less: Standard deduction (new regime) = Rs.75,000. Less: 80CCD(2) eligible deduction (within the 14% new-regime limit) = Rs.1,40,000. Net taxable salary = 15,00,000 + 1,40,000 - 75,000 - 1,40,000 = Rs.14,25,000. The Trap: Candidates who omit the add-back of the employer NPS contribution before allowing the 80CCD(2) deduction reach Rs.12,85,000 (option C). Forgetting the standard deduction entirely gives Rs.15,00,000 (option A). Applying the old-regime 10% limit gives Rs.13,60,000 (option D). Note: The add-back and the 80CCD(2) deduction offset each other when the employer contribution is within the 14% new-regime ceiling, so the net effect on taxable salary is simply gross salary minus the standard deduction.
